body:
## Summary

Improve Florence-2 caption quality by feeding the new scoring system's outputs (Subject tag, Photo Type tag, YOLO detections, exposure style) as grounding prompts. Strict quality win at near-zero compute cost.

## Context

This was identified during the scoring system redesign (see `docs/architecture/scoring-module-contracts.md`). Once the two-axis tag system lands, every image will already have:

- Subject tag (one of 16)
- Photo Type tag (one of 12)
- YOLO detections with bboxes
- Exposure style (normal / high_key / low_key / silhouette)
- Face count and landmarks

Florence-2 currently ignores all of this and re-derives scene content from scratch — leading to hallucinated content, generic captions, and missed grounding opportunities.

## Goal

Pass the above outputs into Florence-2's prompted-captioning interface so:

1. Captions are grounded in the same scene understanding the rest of the pipeline uses (no contradictions between the Subject tag and the caption).
2. Florence-2 stops hallucinating objects YOLO didn't detect.
3. Captions become richer when scene context is unambiguous (Florence-2 can spend its capacity on verbs, relationships, and mood rather than re-identifying the dog).

## Scope

**In scope:**
- Modify `naming.py` (or the caption-producing module) to construct grounded Florence-2 prompts from the upstream tag/detection outputs.
- Validate Florence-2 actually respects the grounding for the prompt variants we choose (some prompts get ignored by Florence-2).
- A/B comparison: ungrounded vs. grounded captions on a 50-image test set; report on caption quality, hallucination rate, and elapsed time.

**Out of scope:**
- The lazy/cull-gated execution model for Florence-2 (Option C from the design discussion). Tracked separately — depends on the cull pipeline.
- Replacing Florence-2 with templates (rejected — Option A).
- Filename template redesign (separate concern; Florence-2 stops being the filename source in Option C work).

## Dependencies

**Blocked by:** scoring-system refactor merge — needs the new two-axis tag outputs to be available in the pipeline before grounding prompts can be built. See `docs/architecture/scoring-module-contracts.md` for the contracts.

## Success criteria

- [ ] Florence-2 prompt construction wired to consume `GenreResult` + `SubScoreBundle` (or equivalent post-refactor types).
- [ ] A/B comparison on 50 fixture images shows grounded captions are at least as accurate as ungrounded, with measurable reduction in hallucinated content.
- [ ] No regression in KPM-1.2 (Florence-2 inference <= 2.5s/image).
- [ ] Unit tests cover the prompt-construction logic (input: tag/detection set, output: prompt string).

## Notes

- Florence-2 supports `<MORE_DETAILED_CAPTION>` and region-grounded variants — need to verify which respects the bbox priors.
- This is a quality win, not a performance win. Compute cost stays the same per Florence-2 invocation.
title: Florence-2 grounded captioning: feed Subject/Type/YOLO outputs as priors

body:
## Context

FR-1.7.2 introduces multi-genre tagging with a single blended `master_score` computed from a confidence-weighted sum of per-genre GENRE_WEIGHTS.

A wildlife-portrait might legitimately score 4 stars when judged as a portrait but 2 stars when judged as a wildlife shot. The current single-blended scalar collapses that information.

## Proposal

In addition to `master_score`, store and surface per-genre scores:

```python
@dataclass
class FusionResult:
    master_score: float                          # existing — blended
    per_genre_scores: dict[str, float]           # new — score under each detected genre's weight template
    ...
```

XMP:
```xml
<photon:PerGenreScores>
  <rdf:Bag>
    <rdf:li>wildlife=0.62</rdf:li>
    <rdf:li>portrait=0.84</rdf:li>
  </rdf:Bag>
</photon:PerGenreScores>
```

photonforge.db: new column `per_genre_scores TEXT DEFAULT ''` (JSON).

## Why later, not now

Decided in design discussion (2026-05-25): start with single blended `master_score` to ship FR-1.7.2 sooner. Per-genre breakdown is additive — can be added without breaking the blended scalar. Defer until we see whether users actually need the disaggregated view in Darktable.

## Acceptance

- `per_genre_scores` populated for every multi-genre image
- Visible in Darktable Lua plugin as expandable detail next to star rating
- Existing `master_score` field continues to work for legacy queries

## References

- Design doc: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-25-multi-genre-and-back-training-design.md`
- FR-1.7.2 (#67)
title: [Enhancement] Per-genre score breakdown alongside blended master_score

## Context

FR-1.7.1 (genre back-training) collects user corrections from Darktable tag edits. The correction flow is exposed via CLI commands but needs Lua plugin buttons to be usable from inside Darktable.

## Scope

Add three buttons to the PHOTONForge Lua plugin's panel:

1. **Sync Corrections**
   - Spawns: `photo-workflow correct-genres --photon-db <cartridge>/photonforge.db --darktable-db <cartridge>/darktable/library.db --training-db <cartridge>/training_weights.db`
   - Reads tag edits made by user in Darktable, logs deltas to `training_weights.db.genre_corrections`.
   - Surfaces unknown `photon|genre|*` style tags as candidate new genres in `custom_genres`.

2. **Recalibrate Genre Model**
   - Spawns: `photo-workflow training recalibrate --training-db <cartridge>/training_weights.db`
   - Triggers prototype re-blending + LR adapter retraining.
   - Shows toast with new version + held-out F1.

3. **Promote Custom Genre**
   - Lists rows from `custom_genres` with `n_examples >= 10` and `promoted = 0`.
   - User selects → spawns: `photo-workflow training promote --genre <name> --training-db ...`
   - On confirm, the genre is added to the active GENRES list.

## Acceptance

- All three buttons visible in the PHOTONForge panel
- Each spawns the corresponding CLI command and surfaces stdout/exit code in a Darktable status message
- Long-running commands (recalibrate) show progress, not a frozen UI

## Depends on

- FR-1.7.1 (#66) — CLI commands must exist first
- FR-1.7.2 (#67) — multi-genre data model

## References

- Design doc: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-25-multi-genre-and-back-training-design.md` (to be created)

## Purpose

A labeled fixture corpus is required for measurable KPMs that need ground-truth comparison:
- KPM-1.6 (dedup false-positive rate) — needs known-distinct image pairs
- KPM-1.7 (naming validity) — needs images with expected non-trivial caption output
- KPM-1.10 (session grouping precision) — needs images with ground-truth session labels

## Specification

Create `tests/fixtures/corpus/` containing:

**Grouping set (~30 images):**
- 3 sessions of ~10 images each
- Session A: timestamps within 30 min of each other, same GPS cluster
- Session B: timestamps 6 hours after A, different GPS
- Session C: timestamps next day
- Ground truth: `tests/fixtures/corpus/grouping_labels.json` — maps filename → session_id

**Dedup set (~20 images):**
- 10 distinct image pairs (visually different, dHash distance >> 2)
- 5 near-duplicate pairs (same scene, slight reframe, dHash distance <= 2)
- Ground truth: `tests/fixtures/corpus/dedup_labels.json` — maps filename → {is_duplicate: bool, pair_id: str}

**Naming set (~20 images):**
- 20 images with diverse content (portraits, landscapes, architecture, abstract)
- Ground truth: `tests/fixtures/corpus/naming_labels.json` — maps filename → {expected_non_trivial: true}
- The label just asserts the caption should NOT be a degenerate string — no specific caption required

## Format

Use synthetic JPEG fixtures (solid colour + embedded EXIF) where possible to keep repo size small. Real-image entries should be Creative Commons licensed with attribution in `tests/fixtures/corpus/SOURCES.md`.

body:
## Problem

The two-axis taxonomy (16 Subjects × 12 Photo Types) already gives every image **two independent labels** — one Subject, one Photo Type — which resolves the obvious cross-genre cases that motivated the original multi-genre proposal:

- Wildlife portrait → Subject=`wildlife`, Type=`portrait`
- Street landscape → Subject=`cityscape`, Type=`street` (or Type=`landscape`)
- Architectural landscape → Subject=`building`, Type=`landscape`
- Event documentation → Subject=`people`, Type=`documentary`

However, **each individual axis is still single-label** (argmax over its distribution). Real images legitimately occupy multiple positions on the same axis:

- **Subject ambiguity**: a person walking a dog (`person` + `pet`); a child at a landmark (`child` + `building`); a still-life with flowers (`object` + `plant`)
- **Type ambiguity**: an environmental portrait (`portrait` + `landscape`); a long-exposure cityscape at night (`long-exposure` + `architecture` + `night-sky`); a candid street shot (`candid` + `street`)

Single-label-per-axis behavior:
- Discards the full per-axis distribution that `genre_router.py` already computes
- Forces the Stage 6 **region router** (driven by Subject) to choose one routing path even when two would apply (e.g. skip eye-sharpness on a `person` + `pet` image)
- Forces the **aesthetic weighter** (driven by Photo Type) to pull a single weight vector when a blended vector would better reflect the image
- Reduces flexibility for Darktable tag-based curation — users see one Subject tag and one Type tag, not the secondary candidates the model already considered

## Proposed Solution

Promote **each axis independently** to multi-label, keeping Subject and Photo Type fully decoupled per the Stage 6 contract:

1. **Router Output** — `GenreResult` already carries full Subject and Photo Type distributions. Add per-axis top-N lists alongside the existing argmax fields:
   ```python
   @dataclass
   class GenreResult:
       subject: str                              # argmax — kept for backward compat
       photo_type: str                           # argmax — kept for backward compat
       subject_confidence: float
       photo_type_confidence: float
       top_subjects: list[tuple[str, float]]    # NEW: top-N per axis
       top_photo_types: list[tuple[str, float]] # NEW: top-N per axis
       subject_distribution: dict[str, float]   # unchanged
       photo_type_distribution: dict[str, float]
   ```

2. **Stage 6 Region Router** — When `top_subjects` contains multiple entries above floor, the region router runs sub-scores for **each qualifying Subject** and blends results by confidence. E.g. a `person (0.62) + pet (0.38)` image runs both eye-sharpness (person path) and animal-eye detection (pet path), then blends sub-scores at 0.62 / 0.38.

3. **Stage 6 Aesthetic Weighter** — Blend per-Type weight vectors from the `aesthetic_weights` SQLite table:
   ```python
   total = sum(c for _, c in top_photo_types)
   blended_weights = {}
   for type_label, conf in top_photo_types:
       w = aesthetic_weights[type_label]
       for k, v in w.items():
           blended_weights[k] = blended_weights.get(k, 0) + (conf / total) * v
   ```
   Master score remains `min(technical, aesthetic)` — only the aesthetic vector becomes a confidence-weighted blend.

4. **Database Schema** — Two JSON columns, one per axis. Keep the existing scalar columns as the highest-confidence label for fast filtering:
   ```sql
   ALTER TABLE photos ADD COLUMN subjects TEXT DEFAULT '';     -- JSON: [{"label": "person", "confidence": 0.62}, ...]
   ALTER TABLE photos ADD COLUMN photo_types TEXT DEFAULT '';  -- JSON: [{"label": "portrait", "confidence": 0.71}, ...]
   -- existing scalar `subject` and `photo_type` columns are the argmax — preserved
   ```

5. **Darktable Bridge** — Extend the hierarchical tag namespaces already in place (`photon|subject|*`, `photon|type|*`) to write **all top-N labels per axis**, not just the argmax. The Lua applicator already supports hierarchical tags from the two-axis commit — only the writer side changes. XMP gains two sibling sequences:
   ```xml
   <photon:Subjects>
     <rdf:Seq>
       <rdf:li photon:Label="person" photon:Confidence="0.62"/>
       <rdf:li photon:Label="pet"    photon:Confidence="0.38"/>
     </rdf:Seq>
   </photon:Subjects>
   <photon:PhotoTypes>
     <rdf:Seq>
       <rdf:li photon:Label="portrait"  photon:Confidence="0.71"/>
       <rdf:li photon:Label="candid"    photon:Confidence="0.22"/>
     </rdf:Seq>
   </photon:PhotoTypes>
   ```

6. **UI Visualization** — In Darktable users see two independent tag stacks:
   - `photon|subject|person`, `photon|subject|pet`
   - `photon|type|portrait`, `photon|type|candid`
   - Removing a tag from either axis feeds the [back-training pipeline](#66) as a per-axis correction signal — Subject corrections do not perturb Photo Type prototypes and vice versa.

## Selection Strategy

**Recommendation: hybrid top-K with floor, applied independently per axis.**

```python
def select_labels(distribution: dict[str, float],
                  top_k: int = 3,
                  floor: float = 0.15) -> list[tuple[str, float]]:
    candidates = {lbl: p for lbl, p in distribution.items() if p >= floor}
    return sorted(candidates.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])[:top_k]

top_subjects   = select_labels(subject_distribution,    top_k=3, floor=0.15)
top_photo_types = select_labels(photo_type_distribution, top_k=3, floor=0.15)
```

Floor of 0.15 sits below the 0.45 routing confidence threshold but above CLIP noise. Per-axis selection means a high-confidence Subject (single label) can coexist with an ambiguous Photo Type (3 labels) on the same image, which matches how real photos sit on the two axes.

## Modules to Touch

- `src/photo_workflow/scoring_types.py`: Add `top_subjects`, `top_photo_types` to `GenreResult`; keep scalar `subject` / `photo_type` as argmax convenience fields
- `src/photo_workflow/genre_router.py`: Emit top-N per axis from the distributions already computed
- `src/photo_workflow/score_fusion.py`: Remove the temporary 50/50 Subject/Type blend; defer multi-label fusion logic to Stage 6 modules (`region_router`, `aesthetic_weighter`)
- `src/photo_workflow/darktable_bridge.py`: Write hierarchical tags for all selected labels per axis; emit `photon:Subjects` and `photon:PhotoTypes` rdf:Seq blocks
- `src/photo_workflow/photondb.py`: Add `subjects` and `photo_types` JSON columns
- `lua/photonforge/tags.lua` + `applicator.lua`: Already handle hierarchical tags from the two-axis commit — verify they accept multiple labels per namespace
- `tests/test_genre_router.py`: Per-axis top-N selection tests
- `tests/test_score_fusion.py` → Stage 6 module tests: blended region routing and blended aesthetic weighting

## Stage 6 Alignment

This change is a **prerequisite for the Stage 6 modular scoring pipeline** described in `docs/architecture/scoring-module-contracts.md`:

- The `region_router` contract assumes Subject can be a multi-label input
- The `aesthetic_weighter` contract assumes Photo Type can be a multi-label input
- `FusionResult.as_flat_dict()` must surface the argmax of each axis to preserve backward compatibility for `pipeline.py`, `darktable_bridge.py`, and the XMP writer — which is why the scalar `subject` / `photo_type` fields stay

Land this issue before or alongside Stage 6 step 1 (region router extraction). The current 50/50 blend in `score_fusion.py` is a placeholder and should be deleted, not extended.

## Success Criteria

- Images with multi-label Subject (e.g. `person` + `pet`) route through both sub-score paths and the blended score is closer to user expectation than the argmax-only score
- Images with multi-label Photo Type (e.g. `portrait` + `landscape`) receive a blended aesthetic weight vector
- Darktable shows multiple `photon|subject|*` or `photon|type|*` tags on ambiguous images; user tag-removal corrections feed [#66](#66) per axis
- Argmax-only consumers (legacy code reading `GenreResult.subject` / `.photo_type`) continue to work unchanged

## Backward Compatibility

- Scalar `subject` and `photo_type` fields on `GenreResult` remain — they are the argmax of `top_subjects[0]` and `top_photo_types[0]`
- `FusionResult.as_flat_dict()` continues to return the same flat keys
- Database migration is additive (two new JSON columns); existing `subject` / `photo_type` columns unchanged
- XMP gains new sequences; existing `photon:Subject` / `photon:PhotoType` scalar fields preserved

## Links

- **Related Issue**: #66 — Per-axis calibration and back-training
- **Taxonomy commit**: `4fc428e` — two-axis tag taxonomy
- **Module contracts**: `docs/architecture/scoring-module-contracts.md`
- **Stage 6 brief**: `docs/architecture/stage-6-engineer-brief.md`
title: [FR-1.7.2] Multi-Genre Tagging Support

body:
## Problem

Live classification under the old single-axis genre router produced 81% "general" tags (3,770 / ~4,650 images). The new two-axis taxonomy (16 Subjects × 12 Photo Types) reduces the "unknown" sink by routing the failure modes into two independent axes — but it inherits the same underlying weakness: **CLIP prototypes are static and have no feedback loop from user corrections**.

Without calibration, the new axes will degrade the same way:
- Subject axis collapses toward dominant classes (`object`, `person`)
- Photo Type axis collapses toward the broad bucket (`documentary`, `candid`)
- Per-axis confidence stays below the 0.45 threshold → images fall through to "unclassified" on either or both axes

## Root Cause

`genre_router.py` runs dual-axis MobileCLIP classification against image-grounded prototypes (built once by `scripts/bruteforce_prototypes.py` from Unsplash Lite + COCO val2017 + Oxford-IIIT Pet, text-blended at α=0.7). EXIF priors apply independently per axis. **Nothing in the runtime path updates either prototype set based on observed errors in the user's library.** The brute-force calibration produces a fixed set, frozen at provision time.

## Proposed Solution

Support **per-axis calibration and back-training** of both prototype sets:

1. **Per-Axis Prototype Refinement** — Collect user corrections on Subject and Photo Type independently (a user may correct one axis while leaving the other intact). Re-estimate each axis's CLIP prototypes as centroids of corrected embeddings, preserving the exclusive-assignment + α=0.7 text-blend invariants from `bruteforce_prototypes.py`.
2. **Feature Augmentation** — Use `subject_area_ratio`, eye sharpness, face/animal/vehicle presence, EXIF focal length, and shutter speed to boost discrimination — especially on the Photo Type axis where CLIP alone underperforms (e.g. distinguishing `candid` from `street`, `portrait` from `still-life`).
3. **Learned Per-Axis Adapter** — Two independent logistic regression / LightGBM heads (one per axis) trained on user feedback; blend with image-grounded prototypes. Subject and Type adapters never share features after the CLIP backbone — they remain independent classifiers per the Stage 6 contract.
4. **Versioning** — Track Subject and Photo Type prototype versions separately. Allow per-axis rollback if calibration on one axis degrades without affecting the other.
5. **UI Integration** — Expose `subject_confidence` and `photo_type_confidence` as separate fields. Flag images where **either** axis falls below 0.45. Hierarchical Darktable tags (`photon|subject|*`, `photon|type|*`) already surface both axes — feedback collection reads corrections from either tag namespace.

## Stage 6 Alignment

Per `docs/architecture/scoring-module-contracts.md`, Subject is the **region router** input and Photo Type is the **aesthetic weighter** input. Calibration quality on each axis has distinct downstream effects:
- **Subject errors** → wrong sub-score region routing (e.g. eye-sharpness check on a landscape)
- **Photo Type errors** → wrong aesthetic weight vector pulled from the `aesthetic_weights` SQLite table

Back-training therefore needs to report calibration F1 **per axis**, not as a single combined metric, because the two failure modes propagate differently through the scoring pipeline.

## Modules to Touch

- `src/photo_workflow/genre_router.py`: Add per-axis calibration entry points; parameter for prototype source (provisioned vs. user-calibrated) on each axis independently
- `src/photo_workflow/scoring_types.py`: `GenreResult` already carries subject + photo_type distributions — extend with per-axis confidence + prototype version fields
- `src/photo_workflow/score_fusion.py`: Replace the temporary 50/50 subject/type blend with the Stage 6 pipeline once it lands; for now, flag low-confidence on either axis
- `src/photo_workflow/darktable_bridge.py`: Replace planned `photon:GenreUserCorrected` with `photon:SubjectUserCorrected` and `photon:PhotoTypeUserCorrected` (per-axis)
- `src/photo_workflow/genre_trainer.py`: Already exists — refactor from single-axis to per-axis trainers; reuse exclusive-assignment + text-blend logic from `scripts/bruteforce_prototypes.py`
- `tests/test_genre_trainer.py`: Per-axis calibration tests; verify Subject calibration does not perturb Photo Type prototypes and vice versa

## Success Criteria

- Subject axis: < 10% of library on the broadest fallback class (`object`)
- Photo Type axis: < 10% on the broadest fallback class (`documentary`)
- Both `subject_confidence` and `photo_type_confidence` distributions shift right (median > 0.6)
- Per-axis F1 lift measurable on a hold-out test set after back-training on 500+ user-corrected images
- Manual override rate < 5% **per axis** independently

## References

- **Taxonomy commit**: `4fc428e` — two-axis tag taxonomy (16 Subjects × 12 Photo Types)
- **Prototype calibration tool**: `scripts/bruteforce_prototypes.py`
- **Module contracts**: `docs/architecture/scoring-module-contracts.md` — Subject = region router, Type = aesthetic weighter
- **Stage 6 brief**: `docs/architecture/stage-6-engineer-brief.md`
- **Research**: `docs/research/scoring-redesign.md` §4 (Genre Detection) — needs follow-up update for two-axis

## Bug

``is_process_alive()`` in ``runner.lua:113-119`` only checks if the sentinel file (``%TEMP%/photonforge.running``) exists — it does not verify the process is actually running.

If the Python subprocess crashes (OOM kill, segfault, unhandled exception that bypasses ``atexit``), the sentinel file is left behind. The Lua polling loop sees the sentinel and assumes the process is still alive, so it keeps waiting.

The loop only exits when ``idle_count > MAX_IDLE`` (600 iterations at 500ms each = **~5 minutes**) or when the user clicks Stop.

```lua
local function is_process_alive()
  local fh = io.open(get_sentinel_path(), 'r')
  if fh then
    fh:close()
    return true  -- sentinel exists, but process may be dead!
  end
  return false
end
```

## Impact

After a crash, the UI appears stuck for up to 5 minutes with no indication that the subprocess has died.

## Suggested Fix

Cross-check the sentinel with actual process liveness:

```lua
local function is_process_alive()
  local fh = io.open(get_sentinel_path(), 'r')
  if not fh then return false end
  fh:close()

  local pid = read_pid_file()
  if not pid then return true end  -- can't check, assume alive

  if IS_WINDOWS then
    local code = os.execute('tasklist /FI "PID eq ' .. pid .. '" /NH | findstr ' .. pid .. ' >/dev/null 2>&1')
    return code == 0
  else
    local code = os.execute('kill -0 ' .. pid .. ' 2>/dev/null')
    return code == 0
  end
end
```

This verifies the PID is still a running process, and the polling loop would exit promptly after a crash.

## Related

- #19 (Windows kill fallback)
- #9 (stop button delayed)
title: Stale sentinel file causes 5-minute hang after subprocess crash

body:
## Bug

The scan step in ``pipeline.py:289-294`` emits per-file ``scan ok`` events but never emits a ``_progress`` event during processing. The only ``_progress`` is emitted at the very end (line 301) with ``done == total``, jumping from 0% to 100% instantly.

```python
# During the loop — no _progress emitted:
for p in photos:
    ...
    emit('scan', p.name, 'ok', json_progress=json_progress)

# Only at the end:
click.echo(json.dumps({'step': '_progress', 'done': len(photos), 'total': len(photos)}))
```

Every other step (dedup, score, name) emits ``_progress`` during processing so the Lua poller can update ``job.percent``. Scan is the only step missing this.

## Impact

The Darktable job progress bar stays at 0% for the entire scan step, then jumps to 100%. For large folders this makes it look like the plugin is stuck.

## Fix

Add a ``_progress`` emission inside the scan loop:

```python
for i, p in enumerate(photos, 1):
    ...
    emit('scan', p.name, 'ok', json_progress=json_progress)
    if json_progress and i % 10 == 0:
        click.echo(json.dumps({'step': '_progress', 'done': i, 'total': len(photos)}))
```

## Related

- #12 (better logging/progress indicators)
title: Scan step emits no progress — progress bar stays at 0%

## Bug

On Windows, ``M.kill()`` in ``runner.lua:122-136`` can only kill the subprocess via ``taskkill /F /PID``. If the PID file hasn't been written yet (race condition during process startup), ``read_pid_file()`` returns nil and **nothing happens** — the process keeps running.

On Linux, there's a ``pkill -f 'photo-workflow'`` fallback (line 133). On Windows, there is no equivalent fallback.

```lua
if IS_WINDOWS then
    if pid then
      os.execute('taskkill /F /PID ' .. pid .. ' >/dev/null 2>&1')
    end
    -- no else! if pid is nil, nothing happens
else
    if pid then
      os.execute('kill -9 ' .. pid .. ' 2>/dev/null')
    else
      os.execute('pkill -f \'photo-workflow\' 2>/dev/null')  -- fallback!
    end
end
```

## Impact

Combined with #9 (delayed stop), this means on Windows the Stop button can completely fail to kill the subprocess, especially during fast steps like scan where the Python process may start and finish before the PID file is read.

## Suggested Fix

Add a Windows fallback using ``taskkill`` by image name:

```lua
if IS_WINDOWS then
    if pid then
        os.execute('taskkill /F /PID ' .. pid .. ' >/dev/null 2>&1')
    else
        os.execute('taskkill /F /IM python.exe /FI "WINDOWTITLE eq photo-workflow" >/dev/null 2>&1')
        -- or: use wmic/Get-Process to find by command line
    end
end
```

Alternatively, use ``taskkill /F /T /PID`` to also kill the cmd.exe parent and its process tree.

## Related

- #9 (delayed stop during scan)
title: Windows: Stop button silently fails if PID file not yet written

The repo needs a housekeeping pass: migrate living documents into version-controlled markdown, connect the roadmap to GitHub project management tools, and remove build artifacts and abandoned code that are tracked in git.

This breaks down into three workstreams.

---

## 1. Document Migration and Organization

### Current state
Architecture and needs documents live in various formats and locations:
- ``docs/Archive/`` — 4 ``.docx`` files (architecture v3, v4, v5, and a duplicate)
- ``docs/photonforge-architecture.md`` — current architecture (markdown, good)
- ``docs/living-user-needs.md`` — living user needs document
- ``docs/Notes.md`` — misc notes
- ``docs/superpowers/plans/`` — 11 plan files from prior development sessions
- ``docs/superpowers/specs/`` — 11 spec files from prior development sessions
- ``docs/mockups/PhotonForgePanel.jsx`` — stale JSX mockup from pre-Lua pivot

body:
## Feature

A new **experimental, opt-in** feature that uses online AI models to generate creative titles and Darktable edit presets for user-flagged photos. This is intentionally separate from the main offline pipeline and only runs on demand.

## Concept

After the standard pipeline (score -> name -> tag) has enriched a photo with genre, quality scores, descriptive names, and tags, a user can flag select photos for premium treatment. This feature would then:

1. **Creative titling**: Generate polished, creative titles using an online LLM, informed by all the metadata the pipeline has already produced (genre, scores, tags, Florence-2 caption, EXIF)
2. **Edit preset creation**: Analyze the photo's characteristics and generate a Darktable style/preset that selects appropriate modules and parameters for that photo's genre and qualities — automating the initial photo correction

## Architecture Notes

**This feature intentionally violates NFR-2.1 (100% offline at runtime).** It requires network access to call online models. This must be:
- Clearly documented as an experimental/optional feature
- Never triggered automatically by the pipeline
- Gated behind explicit user action (flag + activation)

## Prerequisites (must exist before this runs)

- Scoring complete (genre, sharpness, composition, exposure)
- Naming complete (Florence-2 caption, semantic description)
- Tagging complete (#15, #16)
- User flag set on the photo (Darktable color label or star threshold)

## Proposed Workflow

1. User runs the standard pipeline (ingest -> scan -> dedup -> score -> name)
2. User reviews results in Darktable and flags photos for creative processing
3. User triggers the creative step from the plugin panel (separate button, not part of the standard Run)
4. The feature queries only flagged photos, collects their metadata, and calls the online model
5. Results are written back: creative title to description, edit preset to Darktable style

## Edit Preset Generation (detail)

The goal is to map the photo's profile to appropriate Darktable module settings:

| Photo Profile | Suggested Modules |
|---|---|
| Landscape, well-exposed | filmic, color balance, local contrast |
| Portrait, soft lighting | filmic, skin tone, portrait mask |
| Wildlife, high-sharpness | sharpening, denoise, crop |
| Low-light street | denoise (profiled), exposure lift, filmic |

The online model would receive the photo's metadata and generate a Darktable style (.dtstyle XML) or lua-based preset that the applicator writes to the image.

## Open Questions

- Which online model/API? (Claude, GPT-4V, Gemini — needs multimodal for edit preset quality)
- Should the photo itself be sent to the online model, or only the metadata?
- Darktable style format: .dtstyle XML file vs. Lua-driven module parameter setting?
- Cost/rate-limiting for batch processing of flagged photos
- Privacy implications of sending photos to online APIs

## Dependencies

- #15 (genre to tags)
- #16 (naming overhaul — richer metadata for the online model to work with)

## Scope

This is a design/exploration issue. Implementation should start with a proof of concept on a single genre (e.g. landscape) before expanding.
title: Experimental: creative titling and edit preset generation (online models)

## Feature

The scoring step already computes a genre classification (e.g. wildlife, landscape, portrait, street, macro) and stores it in the DB (``genre`` column in photondb), but this data is never written to the Darktable image metadata. It should be applied as a Darktable tag/category so users can filter and organize their library by genre.

## Current State

- **Scoring emits genre**: ``pipeline.py:470`` emits ``genre=fusion.genre`` in the JSON progress output
- **DB stores genre**: ``photondb.py:54`` has ``genre TEXT`` and ``genre_confidence REAL`` columns
- **Applicator ignores genre**: ``applicator.lua:41-52`` handles the score step but only writes ``rating``, ``color labels``, score notes, and original filename — genre is dropped on the floor

## Proposed Change

### Python side
Genre is already emitted in the JSON. No changes needed.

### Lua side (``applicator.lua``)
In the ``rec.step == 'score'`` branch, write the genre to Darktable tags:

```lua
if rec.genre ~= nil and rec.genre ~= '' then
  local tag = dt.tags.create('PHOTONForge|' .. rec.genre)
  dt.tags.attach(tag, img)
end
```

This creates a hierarchical tag (e.g. ``PHOTONForge|wildlife``, ``PHOTONForge|landscape``) that appears in Darktable's tag list and can be used for filtering, smart collections, and export.

## Notes

- Use a ``PHOTONForge|`` prefix to namespace the tags and avoid collisions with user tags
- Consider a confidence threshold — only tag if ``genre_confidence`` is above a minimum (e.g. 0.5) to avoid noisy classifications
title: Write genre/category from scoring step to Darktable image tags

## Problem

The dedup step is slow for ~100 ARW files. Multiple bottlenecks compound.

## Bottlenecks Identified

### 1. cluster_sessions re-reads EXIF from disk (biggest impact)
``cluster_sessions()`` in ``grouping.py:36`` calls ``read_exif_datetime(rec.path)`` for every file, which opens each ~40MB ARW via ``exifread``. But these timestamps were already read during ingest/scan and are stored in the DB as ``exif_timestamp``. The dedup command loads all rows at ``pipeline.py:334`` and has access to the stored timestamps — it should use them instead of re-reading from disk.

### 2. No dHash caching
``_dhash()`` in ``dedup.py:13`` computes a perceptual hash by opening each RAW file via ``rawpy.imread()`` + ``extract_thumb()`` + ``imagehash.dhash()`` on every run. These hashes are deterministic — once computed, they could be stored in the DB (e.g. a ``dhash`` integer column) and reused on subsequent runs. This would make re-runs and resume near-instant.

### 3. Per-file DB commits in update_stages
``update_stages()`` in ``photondb.py:112`` calls ``conn.commit()`` after every file. For 100 files, that is 100 fsyncs. The dedup command already does its own batch commit at ``pipeline.py:361`` for the session/duplicate updates, but the ``update_stages`` calls (line 357) each commit individually.

### 4. Processes ALL rows, not just pending
``pipeline.py:334`` loads all rows and runs ``cluster_sessions`` on all of them, even when only a few files are pending dedup. Session clustering should be able to reuse stored ``session_id`` values for already-processed files.

### 5. update_stages does SELECT before UPDATE per file
``photondb.py:101-111`` does a SELECT to read the current stages, then an UPDATE — 2 queries + commit per file (3 round trips). Could be a single UPDATE with string concatenation in SQL, or batched.

## Suggested Fixes (priority order)

1. **Use DB timestamps for clustering**: Pass ``exif_timestamp`` from the DB row into ``cluster_sessions`` instead of calling ``read_exif_datetime()`` on each file. Eliminates 100 raw file opens.
2. **Cache dHash in DB**: Add a ``dhash INTEGER`` column. Compute only for files with ``dhash IS NULL``. Eliminates rawpy opens on re-runs.
3. **Batch commits**: Remove the per-call ``conn.commit()`` from ``update_stages`` and let the caller control transaction boundaries.
4. **Skip already-clustered files**: Only re-cluster pending files; reuse stored ``session_id`` for completed ones.

## Related

- #11 (ingest per-file commits — same ``update_stages`` issue)
- #10 (scan resume)
title: Dedup step is slow — redundant EXIF reads, no hash caching, per-file commits

@
## Problem

The current Darktable Lua plugin UI has poor observability during and after pipeline runs:

1. **Log is a wall of text**: The text_view log shows raw lines like [14:32:05] scan DSC00142.ARW [ok] with no visual hierarchy, no severity distinction, and no way to tell what matters at a glance.

2. **No in-panel progress indicator**: The only progress feedback is Darktable's bottom job bar (dt.gui.create_job). In the plugin panel itself, there's no counter or progress text showing e.g. Scoring: 42/100. You have to watch lines scroll by and guess.

3. **Step status is unclear**: Each step just shows last: 2026-05-22 14:30 checkmark next to its checkbox. There's no indication of *currently running*, *pending*, *skipped*, or *failed with error*. After a run, it's hard to tell at a glance what succeeded vs. failed.

4. **No post-run summary**: When a multi-step run finishes, the log just says Pipeline complete. with no summary of what was done (files processed, errors, time elapsed).

## Current Implementation

- **Log**: panel.lua:182-193 — plain text_view, lines appended with table.concat
- **Progress**: runner.lua:228-233 — only updates job.percent on Darktable's job bar
- **Status labels**: panel.lua:169-171 — static last: timestamp labels
- **Log format**: runner.lua:235-236 — [HH:MM:SS] step file [status]

## Proposed Improvements

### 1. In-panel progress label per step
Add a dynamic label above or below the log that shows the active step and count:

Scoring: 42/100  |  Step 3/5

This would be updated from runner.lua whenever a _progress JSON record is received. Darktable's Lua API supports updating label.label dynamically.

### 2. Step status indicators
Replace the static last: labels with state-aware text:

| State | Display |
|-------|---------|
| Pending | -- (grey) |
| Running | Running... |
| Done | Done 14:30 (142 files) |
| Failed | FAILED 14:30 |
| Skipped | Skipped |

Update update_status() in panel.lua to accept richer state info, and have runner.lua call it at step start/end/fail.

### 3. Structured log lines
Format log entries with clearer structure:

- Step headers: --- Step 2/5: score --- (already present, good)
- File progress: [14:32:05] score  42/100  DSC00142.ARW  ok
- Errors: [14:32:05] score  42/100  DSC00142.ARW  FAILED: <reason>
- Summary: include done/total counter inline with each file

### 4. Post-run summary
After run_all completes, emit a summary block:



This requires runner.lua to track elapsed time per step (os.clock() or os.time() deltas) and file counts.

## Darktable Lua Constraints

- No native progress bar widget — must simulate with label text
- UI updates only happen when yielding via dt.control.sleep() (single-threaded Lua)
- dt.print() can be used for toast notifications on completion
- Widget tree is built once at load time; dynamic changes are limited to updating label.label, text_view.text, etc.
@
title: Improve Darktable plugin logging, progress indicators, and step status

body:
@
## Problem

Ingest of ~100 ARW files (~4GB from SD) feels slow. KPM-1.1 targets >= 80% USB 3.0 bandwidth but several bottlenecks in src/photo_workflow/ingest.py prevent that.

## Bottlenecks Identified

### 1. Per-file DB commit (biggest impact)
insert_photo() in photondb.py:95 calls conn.commit() after every single file. Each commit forces an fsync to disk. For 100 files that is 100 fsyncs — significant overhead. Batching commits (e.g. every 10-20 files, or wrapping the whole loop in a transaction) would dramatically reduce this.

### 2. Silent EXIF reading phase (perceived slowness)
Before any copying starts, _read_exif_timestamp() is called for every source file (line 94-95) to sort by timestamp and check for already-ingested files. For 100 ARW files on an SD card, this involves 100 random reads with no progress output to the UI. The user sees nothing happening during this phase.

### 3. Single-threaded sequential copy
shutil.copy2 copies files one at a time (line 119). For large ARW files (~40MB each), there may be an opportunity to overlap EXIF reading of the next file with the copy of the current file, though the single SD card bus is likely the real bottleneck here.

### 4. Double volume label read
get_volume_label(dest) is called both in pipeline.py:244 and again in ingest.py:78. Minor, but unnecessary I/O.

## Suggested Fixes (in priority order)

1. **Batch DB commits**: Use conn.execute() without per-file commit, then conn.commit() every N files or at the end. Wrap in a transaction for atomicity.
2. **Emit progress during EXIF phase**: Add a progress emission pass so the UI shows Reading EXIF 1/100... before copying starts.
3. **Consider shutil.copy2 buffer size**: The default buffer may not be optimal for large files over USB. shutil.copyfileobj with a larger buffer (e.g. 1MB) could help.
4. **Remove duplicate volume label call**.

## Environment

- ~100 Sony ARW files (~40MB each)
- SD card reader on Yoga 910 (USB 3.0)
- Destination: external SSD (PHOTON cartridge)
@
title: Ingest step is slow — per-file commits, no parallelism, silent EXIF phase

body:
@
## Bug

After stopping the pipeline mid-scan and resuming, the scan step restarts from file 0 instead of continuing where it left off.

## Root Cause

The scan command in src/photo_workflow/pipeline.py:270-301 iterates over ALL files in the source directory unconditionally. It uses INSERT OR IGNORE so the DB isn't corrupted, but every file is re-read for EXIF and re-emitted as progress — wasting time and resetting the UI counter to 0.

By contrast, dedup, score, and name all call get_pending(conn, table, stage) to skip files that already completed that stage. Scan is the only step missing this pattern.

Additionally, the Lua build_cmd() in lua/photonforge/runner.lua:52-59 explicitly excludes scan from both --resume and --force flags.

## Expected Behavior

On resume, scan should skip files already present in the DB with the scan stage completed, and start progress from the correct offset.

## Suggested Fix

**Python side** (pipeline.py):
- Use get_pending(conn, table, 'scan') or equivalent to get only un-scanned files
- Set progress total/done relative to remaining work

**Lua side** (runner.lua):
- No changes needed if Python handles it — scan is inherently idempotent via INSERT OR IGNORE

## Related

- #9 (delayed stop during scan)
@
title: Scan step does not support resume — restarts from file 0

body:
@
## Bug

Pressing the **Stop** button during the scan step does not stop processing promptly. Stop was pressed at file 8, but the plugin continued processing until file 100.

## Root Cause

Two contributing factors in lua/photonforge/runner.lua:

1. **No abort check inside line-processing loop** (lines 225-243): The inner for line in new_data:gmatch(...) loop processes ALL buffered log output in a single pass without ever checking M.abort. Since dt.control.sleep(500) yields for 500ms between polls, a fast step like scan can buffer hundreds of lines of output. All of those lines get processed and displayed before the next while not M.abort check at the top of the loop.

2. **Windows process kill race**: Even after taskkill /F /PID terminates the Python process, output already flushed to the log file is still consumed by the next poll iteration.

## Expected Behavior

Processing should stop within 1-2 files of pressing the Stop button.

## Suggested Fix

- Check M.abort inside the line-processing for loop and break out immediately
- After the while loop exits on abort, skip processing any remaining buffered log output

## Repro

1. Configure scan with a folder containing 100+ files
2. Run the pipeline with scan enabled
3. Press Stop around file 8
4. Observe log continues to file ~100

## Environment

- Darktable 5.4.1 on Windows 11
- Lua plugin in lua/photonforge/
@
title: Lua plugin: Stop button delayed during scan step
